design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER — task 0 of income_annuity_payouts_and_survivorship (env_0044, category income).

[Step 0 — draw, snapshot, thesis] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 6, 6]}. Occupied before this task: nothing (task 0 is the first). Claimed here: income_ext_beneficiary_arrears (6 factors, tool pay_beneficiary_arrears_076c3375, agent), income_ext_commutation_election (6 factors, tool elect_commuted_value_be644418, owner=user), income_ext_commuted_value_payout (4 factors, tool pay_commuted_value_cb4f45b9, agent). Headroom left for task 1 (draw 2 prerequisites, factors [6,4,4]): the whole joint-and-survivor line — held installments after a first death, post-death deposits at the joint amount and their repayment, survivor releases — none of which this task touches (this task lives on a period-certain contract with a beneficiary payee). Thesis: the surface goal is "take the rest of my late father's annuity as one lump sum"; the scored core is the net lump sum sent (income_ext_commuted_value_payout.net_paid_amount); between them sit two prerequisite sentences: the payout waits on an approved commutation election (which the beneficiary must sign herself), and the commuted value is fixed only after every certain installment that fell due since the death stands issued — and the ledger shows the 2026-08-12 installment was never paid. Depth: 3 writes in a forced chain. Breadth: the cost basis of the Ashgrove deferred fixed annuity annuitized into the contract (the fixed-annuity product of the deferred_annuity_withdrawals_and_death_benefits difficulty), the federal withholding history of the last 12 months, the claim's proof and approval dates, the issue state, the contract's age, the cost-of-living anniversaries, the certain period end date.

[Problem-tree card] root = income_ext_commuted_value_payout. Edge 1: income_ext_commuted_value_payout -> income_ext_commutation_election, kind value_input, gate binding `commuted` (also feeds `elected_rate`), form state, prerequisite sentence (negated direction) "The commuted value is not paid until a commutation election signed by the beneficiary stands approved on the contract." Four-point test: ordering connective "not ... until"; waits on a record-visible state (an approved commutation election on the service requests); no tool/id/code token; hard requirement exactly as intended. Exactly one write of this difficulty creates an approved commutation election: elect_commuted_value_be644418 (owner=user, the beneficiary signs). Opening falsity: initial_state.income_service_requests holds only a death_claim, a withholding_election (Harold, 2011) and a bank_change — no commutation_election. Resolving action: the beneficiary's signed election, handed over by the agent. Edge 2: income_ext_commutation_election -> income_ext_beneficiary_arrears, kind value_input, gate `unpaid_past`, form state, sentence (affirmative direction) "The commuted value is fixed only after every certain installment that fell due between the date of death and the approval of the death claim stands issued to the beneficiary on the contract's activity history." Four-point test passes the same way; the only write that issues a certain installment for a past payment date is pay_beneficiary_arrears_076c3375. Opening falsity: death 2026-07-27 (initial_state.income_holdings.<contract>.first_death_date); issued rows exist for 2026-07-12 (to Harold) and 2026-09-12 (to Claire) but none for 2026-08-12 — the claim arrived 2026-08-10 (payments stop on notice) and the beneficiary continuation began with 2026-09-12. Topological order: arrears -> election -> payout (a chain; no parallel edges, so order is fully pinned by the two sentences). Deletion sensitivity (actual run): skipping the arrears write leaves unpaid_past = 1 and the commuted value becomes 12471.49 instead of 11932.61 (the unpaid installment is added undiscounted at 538.88); skipping the election leaves no commuted value at all (the payout compute has nothing to pay — LATEST returns no election — and the terminal state lacks the election row). user_scenario names no prerequisite: Claire only asks for a lump sum; the August installment and the election appear only as passive if-branches after the agent raises them. The tools validate no prerequisite: all three bodies are plain ctx.create/ctx.update writes with no status, ordering or eligibility check (see task_tools.py).

[Base-invariant card] pay_beneficiary_arrears writes income_payment_issued -> governed by income_payment_schedule; gate payable_status "An installment is issued only while the contract status is income_active, death_claim_pending, survivor_continuing or beneficiary_continuing." — holding status beneficiary_continuing at the handling time (system record, correlated by income_contract_id). The commutation election and the payout both realise income_commuted_value_paid -> governed by income_death_of_annuitant; gate proof_and_approval (death claim with death_certificate_received true and request_status approved, received 2026-08-10, decided 2026-08-24) and gate lump_sum_status (status beneficiary_continuing is in the allowed set). No time gate governs these subjects (the only time eligibility of the charter is the free-look window), so temporal_feasibility is empty. Commutation eligibility retained in the extended rule: the tier allows beneficiary commutation (Ashgrove Income Annuity 20-Year Certain: beneficiary_commutation_allowed true) and at least commutation_min_remaining_payments (12) installments remain — 24 payment dates from 2026-10-12 to 2028-09-12.

[Business-object card] Target: contract IA50731846 (20-Year Certain, owner/annuitant Harold James Brennan, payee Claire Brennan-Ortiz). Correlation keys: income_contract_id for every write; the death claim income_request_id for the election; the election's own reference number (returned by the election receipt, ireq_0789dc2a66f8) for the payout. Rows aggregated: the 13 issued installments (2025-08-12..2026-07-12 to Harold, 2026-09-12 to Claire) for the 12-month federal withholding test (only due dates within the last 12 months count: 2025-10-12 onward, 431.63) and for the count of installments issued since the death; the last installment issued to the annuitant (2026-07-12, 538.88). Excluded by key: the 2008 purchase row, the designation line, the 2025-08-12 and 2025-09-12 rows for the 12-month window (outside it). Nothing already settled overlaps: no refund, commutation or overpayment rows exist.

[Factor card — income_ext_beneficiary_arrears, 6 factors, result 469.81] (1) arrears_installment_amount (method): a cost-of-living increase took effect on the 2026-09-01 anniversary after the 2026-07-27 death and no installment is held -> paid at the last installment issued to Harold, 538.88; baseline (current installment 544.27) gives 474.51. (2) arrears_investment_in_contract (method, cross-difficulty fixed): the contract was bought by annuitizing Harold's Ashgrove Flexible Premium Deferred Annuity FA50218837 (fixed_holdings cost_basis 41500.00); tax-free already recovered = (78600.00 - (-28048.59)) x 0.6660 = 71027.96 > 41500.00, so nothing of the installment is tax-free; baseline (purchase amount 78600.00) leaves 358.89 tax-free and gives 520.06. (3) arrears_withholding_rate (parameter): Claire is the payee, not the owner, and has no election of her own (the only election on file is Harold's 0.07 of 2011-12-19) -> payee default 0.10; baseline 0.07 gives 485.98. (4) arrears_interest_rate (parameter, multi-source: issue state AND days since proof): NY contract and 58 days since proof (2026-08-10) > 30 -> group delay rate 0.06; baseline 0.035 gives 467.15. (5) arrears_interest_period (method): NY -> from the date of death, 72 days; baseline from proof, 58 days, gives 468.57. (6) arrears_state_tax (parameter): NY and federal tax withheld now and in the last 12 months (431.63) -> the alternative state rate 0.04 on the taxable 538.88 = 21.56; baseline none gives 491.37. All-baseline fall-back: 534.57. Near-miss: the 2025-09-12 installment (37.72 withheld) sits exactly outside the 12-month window; Harold's 2011 withholding election is on file but is not the payee's own.
[Factor card — income_ext_commutation_election, 6 factors, result 11932.61] (1) commuted_installment_count (method): status beneficiary_continuing -> 24 payment dates from 2026-10-12 to 2028-09-12, unissued past installments 0 after the arrears write; baseline 240 - 214 = 26 gives 12927.32. (2) commutation_cutoff_installment (method): next payment 2026-10-12 is 5 days away (<= 10) -> left out, 23 commuted; baseline gives 12420.94. (3) commutation_spread_by_term_left (parameter): 23 months left (< 24) -> 0.0050; baseline 0.0100 gives 11893.17. (4) commutation_rate_floor_and_cap (parameter, multi-source: months in force AND rate): in force 217 months (>= 120) and 0.0485 + 0.0050 = 0.0535 < 0.0550 -> floor 0.0550; baseline 0.0535 gives 11949.60. (5) commutation_first_discount_period (method): 5 days <= 10 -> first commuted (2026-11-12) discounted (5 + 30.4375)/30.4375 = 1.16427 periods; baseline 1 period gives 11941.36. (6) commutation_cost_of_living_growth (method): cola 0.01 and 23 months left (< 36) -> segments 10 at 544.27, 12 at +1 percent, 1 at +2 percent; baseline level gives 11862.10. All-baseline fall-back: 13282.65. Near-miss: the 2026-10-12 installment is the trap a careless reader commutes.
[Factor card — income_ext_commuted_value_payout, 4 factors, result 9068.79] (1) commuted_value_taxable_part (method): non-qualified and investment unrecovered = 41500.00 - 71386.86 = -29886.86 (recovered at the payout's handling time, after the arrears payment lowered the unreturned purchase amount to -28587.47) -> whole 11932.61 taxable; baseline (exclusion ratio 0.6660) gives 10976.09. (2) commuted_value_investment_in_contract (method, cross-difficulty fixed): basis 41500.00 of fixed annuity FA50218837; baseline purchase amount makes 7213.14 still unrecovered (taxable 4719.47) and gives 10799.94. (3) commuted_value_withholding_rate (parameter): the election carries Claire's 0.20 -> 2386.52; baseline 0.07 gives 10620.03. (4) commuted_value_state_tax (parameter): NY alternative state rate 0.04 of the taxable 11932.61 = 477.30; baseline gives 9546.09. All-baseline fall-back 11653.63.
Inherited, not re-legislated: payable_status, proof_and_approval, lump_sum_status, the commutation-minimum and allow flag; declared overrides (overwrite) only: the exclusion-ratio sentence and the withholding sentence of income_payment_schedule (both for the arrears and both for the payout), and the commuted-value sentence of income_death_of_annuitant (election).

[Seed rows and why] customers: Claire (caller, identity), Harold (owner; his profile is reached through the indexed lookup by his customer number). income_holdings: the contract (status, dates, cola, ratio, unreturned_premium cache -28048.59 = 78600.00 - 106648.59 gross paid since 2008, carried as the cache because only the last 13 installments are seeded). income_transactions: purchase row, designation line (Claire primary 100 percent), 13 issued installments (fully taxable, as the recovered investment requires; Harold at 7 percent, Claire at the 10 percent payee default). income_service_requests: approved death claim (proof 2026-08-10, approved 2026-08-24, certificate on file), Harold's 2011 withholding election, Claire's 2026-08-24 bank change. fixed_holdings/transactions: FA50218837 (Flexible Premium Deferred Annuity, issued 1996-05-20) annuitized 2008-09-01 with cost_basis 41500.00, premium 1996-05-20 and the annuitization transfer of 78600.00. Removing the fixed row moves the arrears and payout results (factor 2 / factor 2); removing the 2026-09-12 row changes the payee-continuation evidence and the 12-month sum; removing the death claim removes the proof date. Automatic clauses checked: no proof-of-life request is due (Harold died before the 2026-09-01 anniversary at age 90), no suspension, no held balance, no overpayment (no deposit after the death went to Harold).

[Persona design] Claire, a tired but courteous retired librarian, volunteers only her name, phone and the lump-sum wish, gives date of birth and SSN last four only when asked, answers the must-ask questions (withholding 20 percent, direct deposit, contract number, email/address), and reacts passively to the arrears explanation and the hand-over of the election. She never mentions August, the election mechanics or any amount.

[Standard solution] find_customers(name, phone) -> verify (DOB, SSN4, phone) -> contract by payee_customer_id -> service requests -> activity -> Harold's fixed annuity contract and its activity -> unlock+call pay_beneficiary_arrears (2026-08-12, 538.88 gross, 469.81 net) -> unlock_user + Claire calls elect_commuted_value (commuted 11932.61, 0.20, direct_deposit) -> unlock+call pay_commuted_value (election ireq_0789dc2a66f8, 11932.61 gross, 9068.79 net).

[Verification run] /tmp authoring script replays the gold writes with the real tools and evaluates each compute on the handling-time world: X0 469.81 at step 8, E0 11932.61 at step 10 (after the arrears write), P0 9068.79 at step 12 (after the election); per-factor and all-baseline figures as listed; prerequisite skips as listed. The gates check_compute / check_extended / check_solvability / replay_tasks / check_grounding / check_cross_fire were run per task (outputs in the closing record).

[Draft recomputation from the visible context] From the published rules, the tool schemas, the persona and the lookups alone: the payout rule says nothing is paid until an approved election exists -> none on file -> the election rule says the value is fixed only after every installment since the death is issued -> the activity shows 2026-07-12 then 2026-09-12 with the death on 2026-07-27 -> 2026-08-12 is missing -> pay it under the arrears rule -> compute the commuted value -> hand the election to Claire -> pay the net. Same objects, order and figures as gold.

[Revision 2 — policy-task audit round 1, items closed]
F1: the payout policy now declares the base exclusion-ratio sentence of income_payment_schedule as superseded, replaced by its own taxable-part sentence (investment = annuitized cost basis); the base purchase-amount cap is no longer an equally sourced reading. Payout net unchanged in method (now 9068.79 after F5).
F3 (round 2 change, superseded in revision 4 below): arrears tier 1 was changed to raise the last installment issued to the annuitant once for each contract anniversary falling after the death and on or before the first payment date after the death. The audit showed this still disagreed with the base cost-of-living sentence in other worlds. On this world no anniversary falls between 2026-07-27 and 2026-08-12, so the arrears installment stays 538.88 (anniversaries_to_arrears_date = 0).
F5: every state-tax tier is now a rate on the taxable part (flat rate 0.05 for IA/MN/NC/VT, alternative rate 0.04 for DE/NY/OK, else none) — one formula, the tier selecting the rate, so the `parameter` label is honest; the payout keeps two honest parameter factors (withholding rate, state tax). NY now gives arrears state tax 0.04 x 538.88 = 21.56 (net 469.81) and payout state tax 0.04 x 11932.61 = 477.30 (net 9068.79).
F6: the arrears interest-period tier that ran interest from a late approval date is replaced by the date-of-notice rule: for a contract issued outside the interest group, interest runs from the date the death was first reported to Ashgrove when that report preceded due proof; otherwise from the date due proof was received. This world (NY, no prior death report) stays on the date-of-death tier (72 days).
F7: Harold's annuitized source contract is now his Ashgrove Flexible Premium Deferred Annuity FA50218837 (fixed_holdings, cost_basis 41500.00, premium 1996-05-20, annuitized 2008-09-01 for 78600.00), a product the deferred_annuity_withdrawals_and_death_benefits difficulty claims; purchase_source ashgrove_fixed_annuitization, and the cross_difficulty label of the arrears and payout investment factors is `fixed`. Reads 5-6 are now find_fixed_annuity_contracts(Harold) and find_fixed_annuity_activity.
Observations closed in passing: O-1 (proof date now requires the certificate received), O-4 (edge conditions match the sentences word for word), O-5 (the election receipt no longer says what the reference number is needed for; the payout tool's election argument now points to the service-request lookup or receipt), and the persona line previewing the cutoff installment was removed.
Re-run of the factor sensitivities on the new world (actual output): arrears 469.81 — installment 474.51, investment 520.06, withholding 485.98, interest rate 467.15, interest period 468.57, state tax 491.37, all-baseline 534.57; election 11932.61 unchanged (12927.32 / 12420.94 / 11893.17 / 11949.60 / 11941.36 / 11862.10, all-baseline 13282.65; skipping the arrears gives 12471.49); payout 9068.79 — taxable part 10976.09, investment 10799.94, withholding 10620.03, state tax 9546.09, all-baseline 11653.63.

[Revision 3 — policy-task audit revision_2, items closed]
F3 (residual): the arrears policy now identifies its own installment and prices it at the amount in force on its own payment date. The rule says the arrears installments are paid one at a time, earliest payment date first, so the installment being paid is the earliest certain installment that fell due after the death with no issued payment. Tier 1 raised the last installment issued to the annuitant once for each contract anniversary falling after the death and on or before that installment's own payment date. The audit's revision_3 counter-example showed this still drops an anniversary falling between that last installment and the death, so the round-3 claim of full agreement with the base sentence was wrong; corrected in revision 4 below. The compute finds the position by testing each post-death payment date (months from the first payment date) for an issued row, and reads the anniversary count to that date. Probe run on the audit's example (death 2026-07-27, both 2026-08-12 and 2026-09-12 unpaid): first arrears 538.88 (zero anniversaries); after it is issued, the second arrears is 544.27 (one anniversary, 2026-09-01), equal to base. On this world the arrears installment is 2026-08-12 and every figure is unchanged (gross 538.88, net 469.81, factor figures 474.51 / 520.06 / 485.98 / 467.15 / 468.57 / 491.37, all-baseline 534.57).
O-1 (a): the held-amount tier now reads only what is still held for the arrears installment's own payment date (held entries for that date less releases for that date), not the latest held row on the contract.
O-11: the release now names the overpayment-recovery sentence "Held installments falling due after the death are forfeited rather than paid …" as superseded, and the repayment names "An installment paid … is an overpayment, recorded once per installment" as superseded (task 1 policies; text only, no figure moves).

[Revision 4 — policy-task audit revision_3, items closed]
F3: tier 1 now counts every contract anniversary falling after the payment date of the last installment issued to the annuitant, not after the date of death, and on or before the arrears installment's own payment date. The tier fires when an anniversary has taken effect since that last installment. The last installment is raised by the cost-of-living rate once for each such anniversary, rounded to the cent after each increase, which is how the base schedule builds each contract year's installment. The base cost-of-living sentence is now also declared in the arrears overwrite. Its replacement states the same counting, plus the one residual difference: beyond twelve increases since the last annuitant installment, the further increases are compounded in one step. That situation would need more than twelve years without any installment issued to the annuitant. So no world is left with an undeclared second reading.
Probe runs with the policy compute:
- This world: 2026-08-12 arrears, last annuitant installment 2026-07-12, no anniversary between -> 538.88 (net 469.81, unchanged).
- The audit's two-arrears case: 538.88, then 544.27.
- The audit's revision_3 counter-example: last annuitant installment 2026-08-12 at 538.88, anniversary 2026-09-01, death 2026-09-05, arrears 2026-09-12, NOW 2027-09-20 -> one anniversary counted -> 544.27, equal to base.
O-20: the position search now covers the first six payment dates after the death and counts a date only once it has fallen due (a date in the future is never taken as unpaid). With no unpaid due date among the six, the first post-death date is taken.
O-19: the repayment sentence now restores the record-once rule for every tier: "An overpayment on a deposit paid after a death is recorded once against that deposit; on a joint-and-survivor tier the overpayment on a deposit paid after the first death is the part of it the surviving payee was not entitled to." The release rule now also says "no part of a held installment is ever counted as an overpayment". Both are text only for task 1: no figure moves.
All task 0 figures are unchanged: arrears 469.81 (474.51 / 520.06 / 485.98 / 467.15 / 468.57 / 491.37, all-baseline 534.57), election 11932.61, payout 9068.79.

[Revision 5 — policy-task audit revision_4, item F8 closed at its root]
F8: the arrears rule no longer searches a capped list of dates. Arrears are now scoped the way the business sees them: the certain installments that fell due between the date of death and the date the death claim was approved, while payments were stopped pending the claim. Installments falling due after approval follow the regular schedule (base: the remaining certain installments continue to the beneficiaries on the original schedule).
- No installment of the span is paid on the regular schedule, and arrears are paid earliest first. So the issued installments of the span are always its earliest ones, and the arrears installment being paid is the first post-death payment date plus the number already issued in the span. That is exact for every world, with no cap and no fallback.
- When the whole span stands issued, no arrears installment is owed and the computation gives 0.
- The election's prerequisite sentence and its count of unissued past installments use the same span ("between the date of death and the approval of the death claim"), so the two policies agree on what an arrears installment is.
Probe runs (policy compute):
- This world: claim approved 2026-08-24, span = {2026-08-12}, none issued -> 2026-08-12, 538.88, net 469.81 (unchanged).
- Revision-2 case (approval 2026-10-01): 538.88, then 544.27.
- Revision-3 counter-example (death 2026-09-05, approval 2026-10-20, NOW 2027-09-20): 2026-09-12 at 544.27, then 2026-10-12 at 544.27.
- F8 case (span fully issued, a later regular installment skipped): no arrears owed.
The O-20 position probes and their six-date cap are gone. All task 0 figures are unchanged: arrears 469.81 (factor figures 474.51 / 520.06 / 485.98 / 467.15 / 468.57 / 491.37, all-baseline 534.57), election 11932.61 (skipping the arrears still gives 12471.49), payout 9068.79.
user_scenario:
You are Claire Brennan-Ortiz, 58, a retired middle-school librarian in Charlotte, North Carolina. You speak warmly but a little wearily; you have spent two months dealing with your father's affairs and you like people to explain things in plain words. Your father, Harold James Brennan, died on July 27 this year. He had an income annuity with Ashgrove that you inherited the remaining payments from, and since September the monthly payment has been coming into your own checking account. You open the call by giving your name, Claire Brennan-Ortiz, and saying you are calling about your late father's Ashgrove annuity: you would rather take whatever is left as one lump sum than keep getting a monthly deposit until 2028, and you would like that set up today if it can be done. You do not know how the lump sum is worked out or what it comes to, and you do not offer any figures.

You give your phone number, 7045550163, along with your name when you first explain who you are. Only when the agent asks you to verify your identity do you give your date of birth, March 9, 1968 (1968-03-09), and the last four digits of your Social Security number, 9142; you give them one at a time as they are asked for. If asked for the contract number, it is IA50731846, from the letter Ashgrove sent you. If asked for an email address, it is claire.brennanortiz@fastmail.com, and your mailing address is 418 Hawthorne Lane, Charlotte, NC 28204. You have not filed any tax withholding form of your own with Ashgrove, and if asked you say so.

You are happy for the agent to take care of whatever Ashgrove needs to do on its side to get this done. If the agent tells you that an earlier installment of your father's annuity was never paid to you and that it will be paid now, you are surprised, say you had no idea, and tell the agent to go ahead. 
When the agent asks how much federal income tax you want withheld from the lump sum, you say you want 20 percent withheld, because your accountant told you to have 20 percent taken out of anything like this. When asked how you want the lump sum paid, you want it sent by direct deposit to the same checking account your September payment went to. You understand that choosing the lump sum is your own decision and that you have to sign the election yourself; once the agent tells you the commuted value and hands the election over to you, you sign it with exactly that amount, 20 percent withholding and direct deposit, and you read out the election reference number it gives you if the agent asks for it.

If a figure the agent gives you seems surprising, you only ask the agent to double-check it against the records; you never suggest a number of your own. When the agent tells you the lump sum has been paid, you thank them, say that is a relief, and end the call.

edges.condition: Every certain installment whose payment date fell after the annuitant's date of death and on or before the date the death claim was approved has an issued payment to the beneficiary on the contract's activity history.
edges.policy_source: The commuted value is fixed only after every certain installment that fell due between the date of death and the approval of the death claim stands issued to the beneficiary on the contract's activity history.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The annuitant died 2026-07-27 and the death claim was approved 2026-08-24; the one certain installment falling due in that span, 2026-08-12, has no issued row (the activity holds 2026-07-12 to Harold and 2026-09-12 to Claire), so unpaid_past = 1.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: pay_beneficiary_arrears books an issued installment for 2026-08-12, so two installments are issued since the death and unpaid_past becomes 0.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain (payout -> election -> arrears) with no parallel edges; each order is pinned by a prerequisite sentence in the blocked policy's own rule: the payout 'is not paid until a commutation election ... stands approved', and the commuted value 'is fixed only after every certain installment that fell due between the date of death and the election stands issued'. Reversing election and arrears changes the commuted value (12471.49 instead of 11932.61), so only one order is correct.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the election leaves no approved commutation election: the payout's commuted binding is empty (the compute cannot produce an amount) and the terminal state lacks the election row; with it the payout is 11932.61 gross / 9068.79 net.

Skipping the arrears write leaves unpaid_past = 1, so the commuted value adds 538.88 undiscounted: 12471.49 instead of 11932.61 (and the payout gross/net follow it); the 2026-08-12 issued row is also missing from the terminal state.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only for the lump sum; it never mentions the August installment, any unpaid payment, an election form or the order of steps. The August installment and the election appear only as passive branches ('If the agent tells you that an earlier installment ... was never paid', 'once the agent ... hands the election over to you').
